content.definition: Revaluing subsidiary's assets/liabilities to fair value on subsidiary's separate books (not just in consolidation)
content.concept: Push down parent's acquisition basis adjustments to subsidiary's standalone financial statements
content.when_applicable: When control acquired (typically >50% ownership) in business combination or change in control event
content.asc_805_election: ASC 805 allows acquired entity to elect pushdown accounting (optional, not required)
content.sec_guidance: SEC registrants: Pushdown required if substantially all (>95%) equity acquired. Optional if 80-95%. Not applicable if <80%.

effect_on_subsidiary_books.assets_liabilities: Adjust to fair value (same as parent would use in consolidation)
effect_on_subsidiary_books.equity_accounts: Eliminate old equity, create new equity reflecting acquisition basis
effect_on_subsidiary_books.goodwill: Recognize goodwill on subsidiary books (if consideration > FV of net assets)

example.facts: Parent acquires 100% of subsidiary for $500K. Subsidiary's BV: Assets $400K, Liabilities $150K, Equity $250K. FV: Assets $480K, Liabilities $150K.
example.without_pushdown: Subsidiary's books unchanged. Parent adjusts in consolidation worksheet.

with_pushdown.subsidiary_adjusts_books: DR Assets $80K, CR Revaluation Capital $80K. Recognize goodwill: $500K - ($480K - $150K) = $170K. DR Goodwill $170K, CR Parent Investment/Equity $170K.
with_pushdown.result: Subsidiary standalone statements show assets at FV, goodwill, and new equity structure reflecting acquisition

content.advantages: Subsidiary's standalone statements reflect acquisition accounting. Simpler consolidation (no worksheet adjustments needed).
content.disadvantages: May not reflect subsidiary's historical basis. Comparability issues with pre-acquisition periods.
content.elimination_of_old_equity: Old common stock, APIC, retained earnings eliminated. Replaced with equity reflecting parent's investment.
content.subsequent_acquisitions: If parent increases ownership (e.g., 60% to 100%), can push down additional adjustments
cpa_exam_tips: Pushdown = Revalue subsidiary's books to acquisition FV (not just consolidation adjustments)
Optional under ASC 805. SEC registrants: Required if >95%, optional if 80-95%.
Adjust subsidiary's assets/liabilities to FV, recognize goodwill on subsidiary's books
Simplifies consolidation (no FV adjustments needed in consolidation worksheet)
Not commonly tested in detail - know the concept

key_points: Pushdown accounting: Revalue subsidiary's assets/liabilities to FV on subsidiary's own books
Optional under ASC 805 (SEC registrants: Required >95%, optional 80-95%)
Adjust assets/liabilities to FV, recognize goodwill, eliminate old equity
Simplifies consolidation by incorporating acquisition adjustments into subsidiary's books
Subsidiary's standalone statements reflect acquisition accounting basis
